articles.title: Preparing for the Fantasy Football Playoffs: Defenses (2026)
articles.author: Ryan Reynolds
articles.summary: Preparing for the Fantasy Football Playoffs: Defenses (2026) Fantasy Playoffs Schedules for the Top Defensive Options Vikings Defense Week 15 vs. Lions (SNF) Week 16 vs. Commanders Week 17 at Jets Steelers Defense Week 15 vs. Ravens Week 16 vs Panthers Week 17 at Titans Seahawks Defense Week 15 at Eagles Week 16 vs Rams (Friday/ Christmas) Week 17 at Panthers Rams Defense Week 15 vs Cowboys Week 16 at Seahawks (Friday/ Christmas) Week 17 at Buccaneers Broncos Defense Week 15 at Raiders Week 16 vs Bills (Friday/ Christmas) Week 17 at Patriots 49ers Defense Week 15 at Chargers (TNF) Week 16 at Chiefs Week 17 vs. Eagles Bengals Defense Week 15 at Panthers Week 16 at Colts Week 17 vs. Ravens (TNF) Texans Defense Week 15 vs Jaguars Week 16 at Eagles (TNF) Week 17 at Packers (MNF) Writeups for the Top Defensive Options Vikings: Minnesota has my favorite mix of general capability, pass rush, high-ceiling matchups and playable weeks in the fantasy playoffs. Week 15 against Detroit is the worst matchup of the group, but even in that one the Vikings are home, against Jared Goff who is, historically, a different player when he’s pressured early and often. The Vikings will have a trench advantage against the Commanders. If Minnesota plays Geno Smith in Week 17, that’s a good matchup against a very pressure sensitive quarterback, in a situation where Aaron Glenn’s coaching staff is either under a ton of pressure, if not already out. If Cade Klubnik is starting that game, from what I saw last week he could take a dozen sacks and turn the ball over multiple times against Brian Flores. Steelers: Lamar Jackson’s injury makes the Steelers a very valuable option for the fantasy playoffs, as they now have a potential smash spot against Baltimore in Week 15. A playable game vs Carolina on what is a very tough slate in Week 16 for fantasy defenses, and a Week 17 game against the Titans where Pittsburgh will have a trench advantage. Seahawks: My concern with Seattle’s defense is they do not have a very good offense this year, and that can put their defense in precarious positions. They have an excellent matchup in Week 15 against the broken Eagles. Week 16 against the Rams, I’d rather not play Seattle unless Puka Nacua and Davante Adams are both still out by then. Week 17 is a solid matchup at Carolina. Rams: I have not been impressed with the Cowboys offensive line for weeks, and the Cowboys defense is so bad in space there’s a real strong chance the Rams could win this game with some distance, so I like their defense in Week 15. The Rams are again playable in Week 16 in Seattle and Week 17 at Tampa, but both the Seahawks and Buccaneers have solid offensive lines, with underwhelming overall offenses, but solid veteran quarterbacks. That said, if the Rams pass rush remains whole down the stretch, this is a high-ceiling unit with 3 solid matchups. Broncos: I like Fernando Mendoza long term, but he is playing behind a volatile offensive line and a limited skill group, so Week 15 at the Raiders is a solid matchup for Denver. I don’t have any enthusiasm for the Broncos defense against the Bills in Week 16, with the caveat that there are very few really good defensive matchups on that slate. Assuming that Drake Maye will be out, Week 17 at New England is a potential smash spot for Denver, and the Broncos Defense is on the short list of groups you’d rather not face in the finals. 49ers: San Francisco has an excellent front, so they have a lot of ceiling against the Chargers, with the caveat that this is a road Thursday Night game, and I could see LA being feisty in that spot. I don’t have much interest playing the 49ers defense in Kansas City, but San Francisco against the broken Eagles is on the short list of defenses you don’t want to face in the finals. Bengals: Cincinnati has benefitted greatly this season from their schedule, and that bodes true in the fantasy playoffs as well. The Bengals do not have a great back end, but they do have a quality four-man pass rush. Week 15 at Carolina is a playable matchup, while Week 16 at the Colts and Week 17 on a short week, at home, against Lamar Jackson-less Baltimore are two potential smash spots. Texans: Houston has not been as good or reliable as they were expected to be coming into this season, but they do still have a high-end pass rush when they are at full strength, and they have a trench advantage in each of these matchups. Week 15 vs. Jacksonville is an average matchup. Week 16 at the Eagles is a good one, with the caveat that it is a Thursday nighter on the road. Houston will have a trench advantage against the Packers in Week 17. Week 15 Top Defensive Matchups Tier 1 Seahawks Defense at Eagles Steelers Defense vs. Ravens Tier 2 49ers Defense at Chargers (TNF) Packers Defense vs Dolphins Broncos Defense at Raiders Chiefs Defense vs. Patriots (MNF) Tier 3 Jaguars Defense at Texans Week 16 Top Defensive Matchups Tier 1 Texans Defense at Eagles (TNF) Bengals Defense at Colts Vikings Defense vs. Commanders Tier 2 Steelers Defense vs. Panthers Week 17 Top Defensive Matchups Tier 1 Vikings Defense at Jets Bengals Defense vs. Ravens (TNF) 49ers Defense vs. Eagles Tier 2 Steelers Defense at Titans Seahawks Defense at Panthers Bills Defense at Dolphins Broncos Defense at Patriots Tier 3 Browns Defense vs. Colts Chiefs Defense at Chargers Jaguars Defense vs. Commanders Week 15 Notes The tiers are pretty self-explanatory, though in this instance I could see any of these tier 2 options being bumped up when Week 15 comes around, especially the Packers if Micah Parsons is back, at full throttle, and Green Bay needs to win to get in. The 49ers and Broncos are on the road, against offenses that could realistically be better in a month. If Drake Maye is out and Tommy DeVito is in (which looks likely, it’s just not official as of when I wrote this), the Chiefs would be a tier 1 option. Week 16 Notes The Week 16 slate has a ton of relatively even matchups, meaning it’s filled with playoff teams facing each other, mediocre teams facing each other, etc. The Texans and the Bengals both have quality pass rushes, facing broken teams on the road, where they could win with some distance, forcing a volatile offense to play a fourth quarter in a negative game script. Brian Flores has made Lamar Jackson look bad a few times over the years, so I could see Minnesota being a real tough draw for Jayden Daniels, considering Washington’s below average line and skill group. Week 17 Notes Tier 1 has dangerous pass rushes, against teams that will be out of it late in the year with volatile quarterbacks. Tier 2 is all road options, where playoff teams face volatile quarterbacks, in average or worse offenses. For Tier 3, the Browns are a motivated team in a bet against the Colts. I could see myself not being crazy about KC at the Chargers when the time comes. Jacksonville will have a trench advantage against Washington, but the Commanders have Jayden Daniels, who is very capable of pulling rabbits out of his hat. Things will almost certainly change as injuries and other developments shift what certain defenses, and their opponents are capable of. But as things stand now, this is my read on the Week 15-17 defensive landscape, roughly a month plus out.
